questions.question: The ardent supporter attended every rally. ARDENT means:
questions.explanation: Ardent describes strong, burning enthusiasm, so it is closest to passionate.

questions.question: Mang Ruben is a frugal man who saves part of his pay each month. FRUGAL means:
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful with money; thrifty is its synonym.

questions.question: Please give me your candid opinion of the plan. CANDID means:
questions.explanation: Candid means honest and straightforward, like frank.

questions.question: The diligent clerk finished all her reports early. DILIGENT means:
questions.explanation: Diligent describes steady, careful effort; hardworking is the synonym.

questions.question: The auditor was meticulous in checking every entry. METICULOUS means:
questions.explanation: Meticulous means very attentive to detail, i.e., extremely careful.

questions.question: The mayor gave a lucid explanation of the new ordinance. LUCID means:
questions.explanation: Lucid means easily understood; clear is the synonym.

questions.question: Her tenacious efforts finally won the case. TENACIOUS means:
questions.explanation: Tenacious means holding firmly to a purpose, which is persistent.

questions.question: The benevolent donor funded the scholarships of ten students. BENEVOLENT means:
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and generous toward others.

questions.question: Mobile phones have become ubiquitous in the workplace. UBIQUITOUS means:
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous means present or seen everywhere at once.

questions.question: A pragmatic manager chooses solutions that actually work. PRAGMATIC means:
questions.explanation: Pragmatic means dealing with matters sensibly and realistically, i.e., practical.

questions.question: The typewriter is now obsolete in most offices. OBSOLETE means:
questions.explanation: Obsolete means no longer in use because newer things replaced it; outdated is the synonym.

questions.question: The fame of the one-hit singer proved ephemeral. EPHEMERAL means:
questions.explanation: Ephemeral describes something that lasts only a very short time.

questions.question: The obsequious aide laughed at every joke of his superior. OBSEQUIOUS means:
questions.explanation: Obsequious means excessively eager to please, i.e., fawning or servile.

questions.question: The recalcitrant employee refused to follow any new rule. RECALCITRANT means:
questions.explanation: Recalcitrant means resisting authority or control; stubbornly defiant fits.

questions.question: His perfunctory review of the document missed several errors. PERFUNCTORY means:
questions.explanation: Perfunctory describes an action done routinely with minimal effort or interest.

questions.question: Clean water is becoming scarce in some areas. The antonym of SCARCE is:
questions.explanation: Scarce means insufficient; its opposite is abundant.

questions.question: The museum displays ancient tools. The antonym of ANCIENT is:
questions.explanation: Ancient means very old; modern is the opposite.

questions.question: Joel was reluctant to speak in public. The antonym of RELUCTANT is:
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling; eager means keenly willing.

questions.question: The generous owner gave bonuses to all staff. The antonym of GENEROUS is:
questions.explanation: Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give.

questions.question: The glass wall was nearly transparent. The antonym of TRANSPARENT is:
questions.explanation: Transparent lets light through; opaque does not.

questions.question: The champion remained humble despite his fame. The antonym of HUMBLE is:
questions.explanation: Humble means not proud; arrogant means overly proud.

questions.question: The neighbors were hostile toward the newcomers. The antonym of HOSTILE is:
questions.explanation: Hostile means unfriendly or antagonistic; friendly is the opposite.

questions.question: The contract's terms were vague. The antonym of VAGUE is:
questions.explanation: Vague means not clearly stated; explicit means stated clearly and in detail.

questions.question: The lethargic patient could hardly leave his bed. The antonym of LETHARGIC is:
questions.explanation: Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy; energetic is the opposite.

questions.question: The taciturn witness answered only in single words. The antonym of TACITURN is:
questions.explanation: Taciturn means reserved and saying little; talkative is the opposite.

questions.question: The villagers were oblivious to the approaching storm. The antonym of OBLIVIOUS is:
questions.explanation: Oblivious means unaware; aware is the opposite.

questions.question: The magnanimous winner forgave his rival's insults. The antonym of MAGNANIMOUS is:
questions.explanation: Magnanimous means generous and forgiving; petty means small-minded and spiteful.

questions.question: The laconic reply of the spokesperson disappointed reporters. The antonym of LACONIC is:
questions.explanation: Laconic means using very few words; verbose means using too many.

questions.question: The sanguine investor expected the market to rise. The antonym of SANGUINE is:
questions.explanation: Sanguine means optimistic; pessimistic is the opposite.

questions.question: The ostentatious mansion was the talk of the town. The antonym of OSTENTATIOUS is:
questions.explanation: Ostentatious means flashy and meant to impress; unassuming means modest and plain.

questions.question: At the seminar, the host told a joke to break the ice. BREAK THE ICE means:
questions.explanation: To break the ice is to make people feel comfortable at the start of a social situation.

questions.question: The exam was a piece of cake for Lorna. A PIECE OF CAKE means:
questions.explanation: A piece of cake is something that takes little effort.

questions.question: Ramon stayed home because he was under the weather. UNDER THE WEATHER means:
questions.explanation: Under the weather means feeling a bit sick.

questions.question: It was midnight, so Carla decided to hit the sack. HIT THE SACK means:
questions.explanation: To hit the sack is an informal way of saying to go to bed.

questions.question: Don't spill the beans about the surprise party. SPILL THE BEANS means:
questions.explanation: To spill the beans is to disclose confidential information.

questions.question: Mia burned the midnight oil to finish her report. BURN THE MIDNIGHT OIL means:
questions.explanation: The idiom refers to working or studying until very late.

questions.question: Ben had to bite the bullet and accept the pay cut. BITE THE BULLET means:
questions.explanation: To bite the bullet is to face a difficult situation with courage.

questions.question: Our supervisor visits the province once in a blue moon. ONCE IN A BLUE MOON means:
questions.explanation: Once in a blue moon means an event that happens very seldom.

questions.question: Stop beating around the bush and tell us what happened. BEAT AROUND THE BUSH means:
questions.explanation: The idiom means talking indirectly instead of addressing the main issue.

questions.question: After years of losses, the owner finally threw in the towel. THROW IN THE TOWEL means:
questions.explanation: To throw in the towel is to admit defeat and quit.

questions.question: Being late again was the last straw for the manager. THE LAST STRAW means:
options: the final problem that makes patience run out
questions.explanation: It refers to the final burden that makes a situation intolerable.

questions.question: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise, since it led her to a better career. A BLESSING IN DISGUISE means:
options: a good thing that seemed bad at first
questions.explanation: The phrase describes something that turns out to be beneficial despite looking unfortunate.

questions.question: By insulting the committee, he burned his bridges with the agency. BURN ONE'S BRIDGES means:
options: take a big risk for profit
destroy any chance of returning or reconciling
questions.explanation: To burn one's bridges is to cut off ties so that going back is impossible.

questions.question: The inspector turned a blind eye to the violations. TURN A BLIND EYE means:
questions.explanation: The idiom means pretending not to notice something wrong.

questions.question: Nobody mentioned the budget deficit, the elephant in the room. THE ELEPHANT IN THE ROOM means:
options: an obvious problem everyone avoids discussing
questions.explanation: It refers to a major issue that people are aware of but avoid talking about.

questions.question: Ang ibig sabihin ng salitang GALAK ay:
questions.explanation: Ang 'galak' ay kasingkahulugan ng 'tuwa'.

questions.question: Ang kasalungat ng salitang MASIPAG ay:
questions.explanation: Ang 'masipag' ay may sigasig sa gawain; ang kabaligtaran nito ay 'tamad'.

questions.question: Ano ang kahulugan ng salawikaing 'Kapag may itinanim, may aanihin'?
options: Ang pagsisikap ay may magandang bunga
questions.explanation: Ang kasabihan ay nagtuturo na ang pagsisikap ay may gantimpala.

questions.question: Ang sawikaing 'bukas-palad' ay nangangahulugang:
questions.explanation: Ang taong bukas-palad ay laging handang magbigay o tumulong.

questions.question: Ang taong HAMPASLUPA ay:
questions.explanation: Ang 'hampaslupa' ay tawag sa taong lubhang mahirap.

questions.question: Ang sawikaing 'balat-sibuyas' ay tumutukoy sa taong:
questions.explanation: Tulad ng manipis na balat ng sibuyas, madaling mapikon ang taong balat-sibuyas.

questions.question: Ang kasingkahulugan ng NAGDADALAMHATI ay:
questions.explanation: Ang 'dalamhati' ay matinding lungkot, kaya ang nagdadalamhati ay nagluluksa.

questions.question: Ang kasalungat ng MAPAGKUMBABA ay:
questions.explanation: Ang mapagkumbaba ay hindi nagmamalaki; ang kabaligtaran nito ay mapagmataas.

questions.question: Ang sawikaing 'kapit-tuko' ay nangangahulugang:
questions.explanation: Kilala ang tuko sa napakahigpit na kapit, kaya ito ang pinagmulan ng sawikain.

questions.question: Ano ang aral ng salawikaing 'Ang hindi lumingon sa pinanggalingan ay hindi makararating sa paroroonan'?
options: Dapat kilalanin ang pinagmulan at tumanaw ng utang na loob
questions.explanation: Ipinapaalala nito na ang taong hindi marunong lumingon sa pinagmulan at tumanaw ng utang na loob ay mahihirapang magtagumpay.

questions.question: Ang sawikaing 'nagbibilang ng poste' ay tumutukoy sa taong:
questions.explanation: Ang taong walang magawang trabaho ay inilalarawang nagbibilang ng poste.

questions.question: Ang kasingkahulugan ng DALISAY ay:
questions.explanation: Ang 'dalisay' ay malinis at walang halo, gaya ng 'busilak'.

questions.question: Ang ibig sabihin ng salitang SALAT ay:
questions.explanation: Ang 'salat' ay kulang o kapos sa pangangailangan.

questions.question: Ang sawikaing 'alog na ang baba' ay nangangahulugang:
questions.explanation: Ang pag-alog ng baba ay palatandaan ng katandaan, kaya 'matanda na' ang kahulugan.

questions.question: Ano ang ipinahihiwatig ng salawikaing 'Nasa Diyos ang awa, nasa tao ang gawa'?
options: Diyos lang ang gagawa ng lahat
Ang tao ay hindi marunong maawa
Dapat magsikap ang tao at hindi umasa sa dasal lamang
questions.explanation: Ipinapaalala nito na bukod sa pananalig sa Diyos, kailangan ding kumilos ang tao.
